properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 8/18/2021
Violation Code: 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
Violation ID: 927034
Permit API: 053-30017
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Harmony Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/18/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to Pennfield Energy's 8/17/2021 notification of a crude oil discharge from a stock tank located at the Milford South tank battery, which is located adjacent to this well site. Per Matt Duckett (field representative for Pennfield Energy) the oil/water separator that serves this tank battery failed and resulted in all production fluids entering the stock tank, which did not have the capacity to hold all of the fluid. Crude oil then discharged from an open vent on top of one of the stock tanks and onto the ground within an earthen containment that surrounds all of the tanks at the Milford South tank battery. The estimated quantity of crude oil that was released has been revised after conducting remediation work. Matt Duckett stated that approximately five barrels of crude is a more accurate quantity of product actually released as a result of this incident. Additional details regarding the release can be found in the 'Remarks/Violations' section of this report. This well is equipped for production with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack's electric box.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/05/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/05/2025
Violation Code: 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
Violation ID: 8248042
Permit API: 123-47821
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2025
Comments: The Loomis B Lease Loomis 7 OG well is the closest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the Loomis B lease. At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the Loomis 7 OG well. The Loomis B tank battery consists of two stock tanks, a produced fluids separator, and one subsurface produced fluids tank located inside earthen containment diking. The conventional wells on this lease were being produced at the time of this inspection. After arriving on the lease I began to inspect the condition of the tank battery. I found that the produced fluids separator and stock tanks in containment were equipped with PVC drain lines to separate any produced fluids that enter the tank battery from either the separator or the stock tanks into the subsurface produced fluids tank. At the time of this inspection, only the PVC drain line connected to the separator was found to be draining produced fluids. At the time of this inspection, the flowing PVC drain line was improperly positioned, as it was straddled on the edge of a cutout hole on the top of the subsurface produced fluids tank. The manner in which the drain line was situated allows the majority of the fluids flowing through the line to be released onto the top of the tank and ultimately onto the floor of the containment area, as opposed to inside the subsurface tank.The specific conductance of the accumulated fluid inside of the containment area measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. The soils below the fluid accumulating in the containment area also measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. A visual inspection of the containment area revealed additional signs of staining and stressed/dead vegetation around the produced fluids tank similar to that resulting from the ongoing release. This evidence is an indication of previous releases inside of the containment area prior to this inspection. At the time of this inspection, it did not appear that the pooling of fluids around the subsurface produced fluids tank were accumulating at a rate consistent with the volume of fluids being released into containment by the PVC drain. This and the evidence of stressed vegetation/oil staining around the proximity of the subsurface produced fluids tank referenced above suggests that the released fluids inside of the containment area are migrating into the soil below. A conservative estimate of a one gallon per minute discharge rate over the greater than 90 minute duration that I was present to observe the release suggests that more than 90 gallons (>2bbl) were released into the containment during this inspection.Sample number 4568-004 was collected from the fluid actively flowing from the PVC drain line and sample number 4568-005 was collected from the accumulated fluids inside of the containment area adjacent the subsurface produced fluids tank. These samples were sent to the DEP lab for SAC 942 analyses. After concluding my inspection, I called Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) at 14:59 and requested that he meet me immediately on the lease. Upon his arrival, I informed Kyle that I discovered a problem with the tank battery. I gestured to the ongoing release of fluids from the improperly placed PVC drain line. Kyle immediately placed the drain line into the cutout in the subsurface produced fluids tank. Kyle then phoned another TMP official to inform them of the release, but indicated that neither he or the other TMP official seemed to be aware of who had pumped the wells on this lease today. I informed Kyle that the release of fluids would be documented in this inspection report and that a Notice of Violations (NOV) would be included.A NOV is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/31/2026 to D & B GAS PROD LLC in Monroeville Borough, Allegheny county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: D & B GAS PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/31/2026
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8287667
Permit API: 003-21624
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Monroeville Borough
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/31/2026
Comments: On August 31, 2026, the Department conducted an inspection of the Oxford Dev 1 Well.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the well site was located in a wooded area. The access road appeared to be stabilized at the time of the inspection. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present and appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.The production tank was located approximately 60 feet southeast of the well head. Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed what appeared to be a release occurring from the production tank onto the ground. A thick orange fluid was observed leaking from near the top of the tank, traveling down the side of the tank, and onto the ground. Orange and dark oil-like staining were observed on the ground in an approximate 2 foot area around the north side of the tank. Conductivity readings were taking in the thick orange fluid on the ground as well as in the dark oil like staining on the ground with readings of 0.39mS, 5.62mS, 5.81mS, and 9.72mS being obtained. These readings appeared elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.32mS.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke to D and B Gas operator representative Brian Bittinger and informed him of the apparent release from the production tank onto the ground. Mr. Bittinger stated that he had sold the well site and has not been out there since approximately November 2025. However, he acknowledged that if the transfer has not yet been approved by the Department he is responsible and stated he would have crews onsite with in a day to remediate the spill.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Comments: On May 7, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3967072 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3967072, it appeared that excavation and remediation work had started onsite as a covered excavation stockpile was observed at the well site.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5). The covered excavation stockpile that was observed onsite during the time IR 3967072 remains, in addition to another covered excavation stockpile at the downslope end of the impacted area. The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank during the time of IR 3965337 remains covered with plastic sheeting, and appears to have been excavated near the brine tank and the downslope end of the impacted area (see photos 7, 8, and 10). Oil absorbent booms remain placed downslope of the covered impacted area (see photo 12). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected downslope of impacted area (see photos 14 and 15).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remediation work remains ongoing and the impacted area remains adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On July 28, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Cowden 6H gas well located on the Cowden 16 well pad in Hopewell Twp, Washington County following IR 4139756, where violations were issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) on site and failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad.Big Dog Energy (BDE) is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 16 well pad, however, according to DEP records, Diversified owns both the gas wells on the pad and the well pad. While on-site, BDE representative Mr. Scott informed the Department that the ERP should be on-site soon. BDE is reportedly now working on formulating the ERP themselves as opposed to having a 3rd party do it for them. During this inspection, the following was observed:An Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance, all information that is required to be posted on the Act 9 sign appears to be BDE's. Both on-site mailboxes which were attached to the Act 9 sign were observed to be empty at the time of this inspection. (Photos 1-3). Violations issued for failure to have an ERP on site are being continued at this time.A graveled access road was observed to lead to the Cowden 16 gas well pad. No erosion and sedimentation issues were observed.The Cowden 16 gas well pad is located behind a chain-linked fence. (Photo 4).3 gas wells and 1 plugged gas well monument was observed on the Cowden 16 well pad. The 6H gas wellhead had a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the 6H gas wellhead at the time of this inspection. (Photos 5-6)A white storage tank was still observed to be on the Cowden 16 gas well pad and not connected for production (Photos 7-9). Therefore, violations issued for failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) are being continued at this time.An area on the left side of the gas well pad was observed to have dying vegetation. Mr. Scott stated that roundup weed killer was applied to this section of the gas well pad (Photos 10-11). Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on site and failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad are being continued for the 6H gas well at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/07/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 977709
Permit API: 083-47206
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/07/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted upon being notified by Bull Run Resources that a crude oil release had occurred from a gathering line located at this well site.Upon my arrival on the well site, Eric Clancy of Bull Run explained that a pinhole formed in a steel gathering line located behind the location (east-northeast of the well, GPS coordinate 41.80141N 78.85587W). It appears that crude oil has been discharging from this pinhole at a minimal rate for an unknown period of time.Bull Run has repaired the failure in the gathering line, which has stopped the discharge. Oil soaked soil that was excavated to locate and repair the line remains staged on the well site. Crude oil traveled alongside the southeastern corner of the location for approximately 30 feet before reaching a roadside ditch that runs along the southern edge of the spur road. Evidence of crude oil was observed across an approximate 125 foot stretch of this ditch. Field screening with a PID meter did not detect appreciable VOC readings downslope of 41.80182N 78.85616W. Oil soaked leaves and a thin layer of oil soaked soil have been excavated from the southeastern perimeter of the well site and the ditch, this material is staged on the side of the road.Bull Run has constructed an underflow dam near the southern corner of the well site and has placed numerous absorbent pads on pockets of free crude that remain in the excavated area where the line was unearthed and in the ditch. I suggested to Eric that an additional underflow dam be constructed in the ditch downslope of the point where crude has thus far migrated as a preventive measure. Additional underflow dams and/or absorbent pads/booms should also be considered elsewhere across the impacted area to improve the initial containment efforts. Finally, Eric and I discussed the potential excavation of additional soil in the immediate vicinity of the gathering line, given the presence of visible product in this area. All methods of containment should be regularly monitored and maintained.At the time of this inspection, it is estimated that approximately 10 tons of oil soaked soil and leaf litter have been excavated and are in need of disposal. Additional soil excavation will likely be conducted throughout upcoming remediation activities. At this time, the evidence available suggests that less than one barrel of crude oil was released and no watercourses were impacted by this release.It is requested that Bull Run provide a remediation plan and keep the Department apprised of any developments that pertain to the cleanup of the remaining residual crude oil associated with this release. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate remediation efforts and determine if additional measures are required.This well is a conventional well, equipped for production with a pump jack. A site ID sign is posted on the jack. The coordinates for this well were updated as part of this inspection.

As such the Department is again requesting maintenance logs for the Production Tanks and a timeline for when the operator is planning to remove or fix the Production Tanks. Based on this inspection, and no received response on information requested regarding the brine release, all violations will remain open. Inspection Date: 10/17/2025
Comments: On October 17 2025 the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Gaut 4 Well Pad in regards to a spill reported to the Department at 9:23am on 10/17/2025 (CTS 393035). Present during the inspection was operator representative Bruce Carpenter.The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that appeared to have all required information. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel, with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site appeared to exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.During the inspection, Mr. Carpenter showed the Department the location of the spill. According to Mr. Carpenter, the spill occurred around 8:00am on 10/17/2025. The spill of approximately 10 gallons of production fluid occurred from a flow line that ran from the wellhead to a gas buster unit. Upon observation of the spill the flow to the line was stopped. Mr. Carpenter stated that clean up crews were on route to remediate the spill. He stated that the gas buster and the secondary containment would be moved so all contaminated material could be removed. He stated that when reconnected, the gas buster and entire flowline would be in secondary containment to ensure another spill does not occur. He also stated that a valve would be added to the flow line so a pressure test could be conducted prior to using the line again.At the time of the inspection, the Department observed the location of the spill adjacent to the gas buster, below the flow line. Saturated/stained gravel was observed in this area. The spill appeared to be approximately 15 feet long by 10 feet wide. It appeared the contaminated area extended under the secondary containment for the gas buster unit. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of the saturated/stained gravel with readings of 17.97mS, 17.50mS, and 5.60mS. It appeared the conductivity readings decreased with distance away from the flow line. A reading was taken just outside the saturated/stained gravel with a reading of 0.04mS. A background conductivity reading was taken away from the location of the spill with a reading of 0.05mS.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Upon inspection of the additional production equipment onsite, the production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. There were no visible leaks with the GPU, and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a.OGI referral is being requested to follow up on current onsite operations. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Comments: On 03/12/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site following violations issued on 12/19/2023 (IR 3662363, Enforcement 423308). I was accompanied by PA DEP Compliance Specialist, George Traister. Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) were issued on 12/19/2023. The violations were issued as outstanding on 01/31/2024 (IR 3704581).The following was observed on 03/12/2024:Conductivity readings were taken within the water and gravel in the tank battery. The valve on Tank 1 looked to be leaking fluid. Crystallization was noted on the valve (Photo 1). The water within the battery around Tank 1 did not display elevated readings (Photo 2). The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. The piping on the drain from the battery has been shortened. The exterior end is capped, and no elevated conductivity was noted on the ground below. The interior end is open, and I recommend that this is also capped. The water level in the battery is close to the edge of the pipe (Photos 8, 9). Stabilization has been added to the earthen berm. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

Comments: On 8/26/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4237718, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. At the time of this inspection, no formal NOV Response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. Since the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. Since the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks. Should have it within a week to install and get transferred to Murphy" (IR 4174382). Comments: On March 23, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Sanns Frank well site. The inspection is separated into 3 inspection reports due to number of photos. This is inspection 1 of 3.The ESCGP (ESG076322011-00) for this site was issued on 8/27/2021 and was set to expire on 8/26/2026, but was terminated on 11/6/2024 (IRs 3862784 and 3863032).There are 8 total wells on-site at this time. The 1H, 2H, 3H, and 7H appear to be completed and equipped for production at this time. The 4H, 5H, 6H, and 8H appear to have recently completed drilling activities and are currently not in production.Act 9 sign is present and complies with 78a55 fabrication requirements. Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and ESCGP plans are all present on site. The ERP and PPC plans include the required components.Wet Pond (Photos 4-5) appears to be functioning properly, no E and S issues observed at this time.The area below the outlet and level spreader of MRC Rain Garden #2 (Photos 8-17) appears to be heavily saturated with lack of vegetation and exposed earth as the water flows towards UNT to Mingo Creek. The water appears to be exiting the level spreader in sheet flow, but appears to be channelizing as it exits the LOD into the tree line. At this time, the water is entering the stream but no active sediment discharge is observed.The access road crossing of UNT to Mingo Creek (Photos 22-25) is observed with CFS installed on both sides of the access road. The CFS appears to have been installed properly but appears to have not been maintained and is failing, allowing mud to exit the access road via undercutting. The mud is observed to continuing down the slope below the access road into a pond of water on the East side, which also continues via channelized flow into UNT to Mingo Creek. What appears to be dust from the access road is also observed on the surface below the access road on the East side and is observed on most of the leaf cover in this area. At this time, no active sediment discharge is observed into the stream.On the West side, it appears that the extent of the dust and mud ends within the rip rap, however some gravel is observed off the access road.The rock apron below Channel 8 and the level spreader below MRC Rain Garden #3 both appear to be discharging stormwater in sheet flow, however the vegetation below both features is heavily saturated and the stormwater appears to be channelizing closer to the tree line, where it eventually reaches UNT to Mingo Creek. This area also appears to be impacted by a two track trail. At this time, no active sediment discharge is observed into the stream.Additional vegetation disturbances are observed along the access road (Photos 7-9, 13). No E and S issues are observed in these areas at this time. The DEP recommends the operator stabilize these areas.A small release of what appears to be a petroleum-based fluid is observed on the access road near the mailbox (Photos 18-19). The DEP spoke to Scott Clark (Range Resources) during discovery of the release. Clark appeared to be leaving the well pad and informed the DEP that he was unaware of the release, but would have personnel clean it up today.The DEP recommends the operator properly dispose of the impacted material and requests the disposal documents when made available. No violation is being issued for the release at this time due to the volume of the release appearing to be below reporting limits.Well equipment on the well pad appears to be contained within secondary containment and no other spills, leaks, or releases were observed on the well pad at this time.Wooden stakes with ribbons attached are observed at several disturbed areas on-site and near UNT to Mingo. The DEP requests additional information in regard to the stakes.Violations for accelerated erosion and sedimentation, failed E and S BMPs, and failure to maintain PCSM BMP are being issued at this time.

Comments: This site located in a grassy field west off Parks Road at the end of a short access, 320' west of residence and the spring used for their water supply. Well set-up for production with a separator, drip and 100 barrel tank in secondary containment. Annual electronic production report submitted through 2023. Will Warful reported on 5/9/2024 that the nipple on the holding tank rotted and leaked the contents of the 100 barrel holding tank into the unlined secondary containment. A vac truck was used to remove the water that remained in the secondary containment. At this inspection more contaminated material was removed from area where the tank was located in secondary containment, part of secondary containment embankment and ~50' northwest of the original release area. Water in the hole excavated northwest of the secondary containment was tested with handheld conductivity meter, the reading was over 4 milli Siemens. Water pooled in the hole where the secondary containment was excavated was ~2 milli siemens. You are hereby requested to continue to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 912278
Permit API: 083-50409
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/26/2021
Comments: This spill occurred sometime in the previous few months but was not reported to DEP. It was noted on a routine inspection by WQSS Rob Bechtel and myself en route to check another site. It appears as though a line leaked and allowed an unknown quantity of crude oil to be released to the site. Some volume flowed off the site and entered a spring run/UNT of Twomile Run. Crude oil was apparent in pools in several areas and fresher product was caught in moss lining the channel of the spring. It then appears to have flowed some 300 feet and entered another UNT of Twomile Run. The operator placed a boom in this stream at some point prior to the discovery of this spill by myself. Some sheen was apparent in leaf piles at this point, but no fresh product was noted. The operator was contacted and they were on the lease at the time. Immediate cleanup options were discussed, including installation of two siphon dams in the initial spring run and use of absorbent pads to catch any oil seeping from the banks. Further inspection will be performed as necessary. Violations are noted.

Violation ID: 8264367

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/10/2026
Comments: On 02/10/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/09/2026 from Greylock (CTS #395045). I was accompanied by Madison Raviart (PA DEP Water Quality Specialist) and Greylock representative Trevor Wood. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/09/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of brine water released onto the pad on 02/09/2026. The spill was identified at 4:00 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 7:13 PM. Gravel and snow was impacted on the pad and the spill was contained to the pad and snow was hand shoveled into tanks containment. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. There was no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1). I recommend these be added to site near the site entrance. The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).Cinders were placed on road coming up to the pad on 02/10/2026 (Photos 3-5). Snow around the containment for the tanks was hand shoveled and put into the containment (Photo 6). The spill originated from a separator on the pad. High pressure caused brine water to come out of the separator and spray onto the pad and tank. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 7-10). Conductivity readings taken in the middle of the impacted area ranged from 2.09 mS/cm-4.55mS/cm (Photos 11,12). Conductivity reading taken in gravel on the opposite side of the entrance in front of separators was 252 S/cm (Photo 13). Conductivity readings taken along tank containment ranged from 709 S/cm-8.61 mS/cm (Photos 14-18).The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of brine water and no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite, violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78A55(I)5I, and 78a66(b)2.

Comments: On December 7, 2018, the Department performed an inspection of the CNX RHL22 well pad site. The site is located in Richhill Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a follow up inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad on 12/1/18, and violations issued on 12/3/18. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was also excavating the PCSM and PCSM collection channel at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. The Department observed elevated conductivity readings in the standing water and soils on the southwest corner of the well pad, as well as the storm water controls for this area. Elevated conductivity readings were also observed off the well pad site on the pipeline ROW and down gradient from both sites during the 12/3/18 inspection. The operator has completed hydraulic fracturing operations on the site and has begun removing the equipment necessary for hydraulic fracturing from the well pad. The operator has reported to the Department that secondary containment will be setup on the well pad to store excavated, impacted soils for disposal and remediation efforts will continue all weekend and into next week on the well pad as well as in the PCSM structures impacted by the reuse water spill.

The inspection was a follow up inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad on 12/1/18, and violations issued on 12/3/18. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was also excavating the PCSM and PCSM collection channel at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. The Department observed elevated conductivity readings in the standing water and soils on the southwest corner of the well pad, as well as the storm water controls for this area. Elevated conductivity readings were also observed off the well pad site on the pipeline ROW and down gradient from both sites during the 12/3/18 inspection. The operator has completed hydraulic fracturing operations on the site and has begun removing the equipment necessary for hydraulic fracturing from the well pad. The operator has reported to the Department that secondary containment will be setup on the well pad to store excavated, impacted soils for disposal and remediation efforts will continue all weekend and into next week on the well pad as well as in the PCSM structures impacted by the reuse water spill.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/13/2020
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 896991
Permit API: 015-23526
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/13/2020
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that approximately 60-70 gallons of diesel spilled to the pad surface. A frac is on-going on this location. Upon arriving on location, I met with company man Josh Lumbardo. He showed me the location of the release which was tarped due to the rain. Mark Patty, HSE for Chesapeake, then arrived. Mr. Patty said that he believed it was an estimated 65 gallons of diesel released from a diesel delivery truck. An estimated 40 gallons of that is believed to have impacted the surface while the remainder was contained on a piece of secondary containment. A portion of pad material was excavated, placed on secondary containment on the pad, and tarped. Mr. Patty said that Creston Environmental was contracted to investigate the release and to take samples from the pad surface. He also stated that diesel was observed leaching out from beneath the rig mats adjacent to the area of the release. Mr. Patty said that the rig mats would likely be removed as soon as the frac was completed, which he estimates will take 10 more days. Then the area beneath the rig mats will be investigated to assess the extent of the impact. Beneath the tarp on the impacted area of the pad, the fluid appeared to have a gray sheen, it felt oily, and had a faint diesel odor. During this inspection, I recommended to Mr. Patty that they install a sump in the impacted area of the pad and remove fluid from the sump and the surrounding area on an as-needed basis.The Department recommends removing as many rig mats as possible adjacent to the impacted pad area as soon as possible, prior to the completion of the frac, to assess the extent of the impact and to remove any material impacted by the release.The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance 78a.66 due to the unknown extent of the impact to the pad surface which undermines the ability to accurately estimate the spill volume.Violations noted.
